sw.R: Atazikwa kama punda aliyekufa. \q Maiti yake itakokotwa na kutupwa nje ya malango ya Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Nó sẽ bị chôn [như] chôn một con lừa, \q bị kéo lê và quăng ra ngoài các cổng Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Nó sẽ bị chôn như người ta chôn một con lừa, \q bị kéo lê đi và quăng ra ngoài các cổng Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Nó sẽ bị chôn như một con lừa chết. \q Xác nó sẽ bị kéo lê đi và quăng ra ngoài các cổng Giê-ru-sa-lem.

decisions.choice: the burial of a donkey: no burial at all; the body is dragged away and left like a dead animal
decisions.reason: A dead donkey was hauled out of town and dumped. To be denied burial was a great disgrace (16:4; 36:30, where the same is said of Jehoiakim: his body will be thrown out to the heat by day and the frost by night).

decisions.choice: how Jehoiakim's death came about is not told
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 24:6 says only that he "lay down with his fathers" and his son reigned in his place, which tells of his death but not of a burial. He died in 598 BC as the Babylonian army was coming against Jerusalem. Nothing in the histories describes the fate of his body.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that it is the dead king's body that is dragged away.

source.text: עֲלִ֤י הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ וּֽצְעָ֔קִי וּבַבָּשָׁ֖ן תְּנִ֣י קוֹלֵ֑ךְ וְצַֽעֲקִי֙ מֵֽעֲבָרִ֔ים כִּ֥י נִשְׁבְּר֖וּ כָּל־מְאַהֲבָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Go up [to] the Lebanon and cry out, and in the Bashan give your voice, and cry out from Abarim, for are broken all your lovers.

en.L: Go up to Lebanon and cry out, \q and in Bashan raise your voice; \q cry out from Abarim, \q for all your lovers are broken.
en.B: Climb up to Lebanon and cry out; \q let your voice be heard in Bashan; \q cry out from the Abarim mountains, \q for all your lovers have been crushed.
en.R: People of Jerusalem, go up to Lebanon and scream; \q shout in the land of Bashan; \q cry out from the mountains of Abarim, \q because all your allies have been crushed.

es.L: Sube al Líbano y clama, \q y en Basán alza tu voz; \q clama desde Abarim, \q porque todos tus amantes han sido quebrantados.
es.B: Sube al Líbano y grita; \q que se oiga tu voz en Basán; \q grita desde los montes de Abarim, \q porque todos tus amantes han sido destrozados.
es.R: Pueblo de Jerusalén, sube al Líbano y grita; \q grita en la tierra de Basán; \q clama desde los montes de Abarim, \q porque todos tus aliados han sido destrozados.

fr.L: Monte au Liban et crie, \q et dans le Basan élève ta voix ; \q crie depuis les Abarim, \q car tous tes amants sont brisés.
fr.B: Monte au Liban et crie ; \q fais entendre ta voix dans le Basan ; \q crie depuis les monts Abarim, \q car tous tes amants ont été écrasés.
fr.R: Peuple de Jérusalem, monte au Liban et hurle ; \q crie dans le pays de Basan ; \q crie depuis les montagnes des Abarim, \q car tous tes alliés ont été écrasés.

sw.L: Panda Lebanoni ukalie, \q na katika Bashani utoe sauti yako; \q ulie kutoka Abarimu, \q kwa maana wapenzi wako wote wamevunjwa.
sw.B: Panda mpaka Lebanoni ulie kwa sauti; \q sauti yako na isikike katika Bashani; \q lia kutoka milima ya Abarimu, \q kwa maana wapenzi wako wote wamepondwa.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Yerusalemu, pandeni Lebanoni mkapige mayowe; \q pigeni kelele katika nchi ya Bashani; \q lieni kutoka milima ya Abarimu, \q kwa sababu washirika wenu wote wamepondwa.

vi.L: Hãy lên Li-ban mà kêu la, \q hãy cất tiếng tại Ba-san; \q hãy kêu la từ A-ba-rim, \q vì mọi tình nhân của ngươi đều đã bị tan nát.
vi.B: Hãy trèo lên Li-ban mà kêu la; \q hãy để tiếng ngươi vang lên tại Ba-san; \q hãy kêu la từ dãy núi A-ba-rim, \q vì mọi tình nhân của ngươi đều đã bị nghiền nát.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy đi lên Li-ban mà gào thét; \q hãy la lớn trong xứ Ba-san; \q hãy kêu la từ dãy núi A-ba-rim, \q vì mọi đồng minh của ngươi đều đã bị nghiền nát.

decisions.choice: the one addressed: Jerusalem, pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: The commands are feminine singular. As often in Jeremiah (2:20-25; 4:30), the city is spoken to as a woman, and the address runs to verse 23.

decisions.choice: Lebanon, Bashan, Abarim: high places to the north, the northeast and the southeast, from which a cry would carry far
decisions.reason: Lebanon lies to the north, Bashan east of the Sea of Galilee, and the Abarim range in Moab east of the Dead Sea; Moses viewed the land from it (Numbers 27:12). From every height around the land the city is to wail.

decisions.choice: your lovers: the allies Judah trusted instead of the LORD
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses "lovers" for the nations Judah courted for help, Egypt and others (2:33-37; 4:30; 30:14), as if a faithless wife ran after other men.

decisions.choice: People of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names who is spoken to, from verse 23 and the context.

decisions.choice: allies
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of lovers stands for.

decisions.choice: Sube ... clama (feminine singular addressee)
decisions.reason: The one spoken to is Jerusalem pictured as a woman (meaning decision m1), so the commands are singular "tú"; Readable names her, as the English does.

decisions.choice: plural address (pandeni, wenu)
decisions.reason: Readable names the people of Jerusalem, as the English Readable does, so the commands become plural; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew singular for the city pictured as a woman.

decisions.choice: "Peuple de Jérusalem, monte" (R), singular
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks to Jerusalem as a woman, "tu" at every level. Readable names the people of the city as the English does, with the collective singular "Peuple de Jérusalem", so the singular address of the Hebrew (and of the English Readable, which has no plural) is kept through verse 23.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem is "ngươi"; "tình nhân" (L, B), "đồng minh" (R)
decisions.reason: The city under judgment is "ngươi" at every level; "tình nhân" keeps the picture of the allies as lovers, which Readable explains, as the English does.

source.text: דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֵלַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּשַׁלְוֺתַ֔יִךְ אָמַ֖רְתְּ לֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֑ע זֶ֤ה דַרְכֵּךְ֙ מִנְּעוּרַ֔יִךְ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־שָׁמַ֖עַתְּ בְּקוֹלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I spoke to you in your ease; you said: Not I will listen. This [has been] your way from your youth, that not you have listened to my voice.

en.L: I spoke to you in your ease; \q you said, "I will not listen." \q This [has been] your way from your youth, \q that you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice.
en.B: I spoke to you while you felt secure, \q but you said, "I will not listen." \q Ever since you were young you have behaved like this: \q you have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice.
en.R: I warned you when life was easy for you, \q but you said, "I will not listen." \q You have acted like this ever since you were young; \q you have never obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Te hablé en tu prosperidad; \q dijiste: «No escucharé». \q Este [ha sido] tu camino desde tu juventud, \q que no has escuchado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz.
es.B: Te hablé cuando te sentías segura, \q pero dijiste: «No escucharé». \q Desde tu juventud te has portado así: \q no has obedecido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz.
es.R: Te advertí cuando la vida te era fácil, \q pero dijiste: «No voy a escuchar». \q Así te has portado desde que eras joven; \q nunca {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has obedecido.

fr.L: Je t’ai parlé dans ta prospérité ; \q tu as dit : « Je n’écouterai pas. » \q Telle [a été] ta conduite dès ta jeunesse : \q tu n’as pas écouté {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix.
fr.B: Je t’ai parlé quand tu te sentais en sécurité, \q mais tu as dit : « Je n’écouterai pas. » \q Depuis ta jeunesse, tu agis ainsi : \q tu n’as pas obéi à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix.
fr.R: Je t’ai avertie quand la vie était facile pour toi, \q mais tu as dit : « Je n’écouterai pas. » \q Tu agis ainsi depuis ta jeunesse ; \q tu ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as jamais obéi.

sw.L: Nilisema nawe katika raha yako; \q ukasema, "Sitasikiliza." \q Hii [imekuwa] njia yako tangu ujana wako, \q kwamba hukuisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Nilisema nawe ulipojiona salama, \q lakini ukasema, "Sitasikiliza." \q Tangu ujana wako umekuwa ukienenda hivi: \q hukuitii sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Nilikuonya maisha yalipokuwa rahisi kwako, \q lakini ukasema, "Sitasikiliza." \q Umekuwa ukitenda hivi tangu ulipokuwa kijana; \q hujawahi kunitii.

vi.L: Ta đã phán với ngươi lúc ngươi đang yên ổn; \q ngươi nói: "Tôi sẽ không nghe." \q Đó [là] đường lối của ngươi từ thuở ngươi còn trẻ, \q là ngươi không nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ta đã phán với ngươi khi ngươi đang an ổn, \q nhưng ngươi nói: "Tôi sẽ không nghe." \q Từ thuở còn trẻ, ngươi đã cư xử như thế: \q ngươi không vâng theo tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ta đã cảnh cáo ngươi khi đời sống ngươi còn dễ dàng, \q nhưng ngươi nói: "Tôi sẽ không nghe." \q Ngươi đã cư xử như thế từ khi còn trẻ; \q ngươi chưa bao giờ vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

decisions.choice: your ease: your times of security and prosperity
decisions.reason: The word is plural, "your times of ease": when all was well, the people saw no need to listen.

decisions.choice: from your youth: since the beginning of the nation's life
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks of Israel's youth as the time of the exodus and the wilderness (2:2; 3:24-25); disobedience goes back that far (7:25-26).

decisions.choice: never obeyed me
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone means to obey them; Readable says so.

source.text: כָּל־רֹעַ֨יִךְ֙ תִּרְעֶה־ר֔וּחַ וּֽמְאַהֲבַ֖יִךְ בַּשְּׁבִ֣י יֵלֵ֑כוּ כִּ֣י אָ֤ז תֵּבֹ֨שִׁי֙ וְנִכְלַ֔מְתְּ מִכֹּ֖ל רָעָתֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: All your shepherds will shepherd [the] wind, and your lovers into captivity will go; for then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your evil.

en.L: The wind will shepherd all your shepherds, \q and your lovers will go into captivity; \q for then you will be ashamed and disgraced \q because of all your wickedness.
en.B: The wind will herd away all your shepherds, \q and your lovers will be carried into captivity. \q Then you will feel shame and disgrace \q because of all your wickedness.
en.R: A wind will drive all your leaders away, \q and your allies will be taken away as prisoners. \q You will be put to shame and humiliated then \q for all the evil you have done.

es.L: A todos tus pastores los pastoreará el viento, \q y tus amantes irán al cautiverio; \q porque entonces te avergonzarás y serás humillada \q por toda tu maldad.
es.B: El viento arrastrará a todos tus pastores, \q y tus amantes serán llevados cautivos. \q Entonces sentirás vergüenza y deshonra \q por toda tu maldad.
es.R: Un viento se llevará a todos tus líderes, \q y tus aliados serán llevados presos. \q Entonces quedarás avergonzada y humillada \q por todo el mal que has hecho.

fr.L: Le vent fera paître tous tes bergers, \q et tes amants iront en captivité ; \q car alors tu seras honteuse et confuse \q à cause de toute ta méchanceté.
fr.B: Le vent emportera tous tes bergers, \q et tes amants partiront en captivité. \q Alors tu seras couverte de honte et d’humiliation \q à cause de toute ta méchanceté.
fr.R: Un vent chassera tous tes dirigeants, \q et tes alliés seront emmenés comme prisonniers. \q Alors tu seras couverte de honte et humiliée \q pour tout le mal que tu as fait.

sw.L: Upepo utawachunga wachungaji wako wote, \q na wapenzi wako watakwenda utumwani; \q kwa maana ndipo utakapoaibika na kufedheheka \q kwa sababu ya uovu wako wote.
sw.B: Upepo utawafukuza wachungaji wako wote, \q na wapenzi wako watachukuliwa utumwani. \q Ndipo utaona aibu na fedheha \q kwa sababu ya uovu wako wote.
sw.R: Upepo utawapeperusha viongozi wako wote, \q na washirika wako watachukuliwa kama wafungwa. \q Ndipo utaaibishwa na kudhalilishwa \q kwa sababu ya maovu yote uliyoyatenda.

vi.L: Gió sẽ chăn mọi người chăn của ngươi, \q và các tình nhân ngươi sẽ đi vào cảnh lưu đày; \q bấy giờ ngươi sẽ hổ thẹn và nhục nhã \q vì mọi điều gian ác của ngươi.
vi.B: Gió sẽ lùa đi mọi người chăn của ngươi, \q và các tình nhân ngươi sẽ bị bắt đi lưu đày. \q Bấy giờ ngươi sẽ hổ thẹn và nhục nhã \q vì mọi điều gian ác của ngươi.
vi.R: Một cơn gió sẽ thổi bay mọi nhà lãnh đạo của ngươi, \q và các đồng minh ngươi sẽ bị bắt đi làm tù binh. \q Bấy giờ ngươi sẽ bị xấu hổ và nhục nhã \q vì mọi điều gian ác ngươi đã làm.

decisions.choice: the wind will shepherd your shepherds: the rulers will be driven off as a wind drives chaff
decisions.reason: There is a play on words: the verb "to shepherd" is from the same root as "shepherds". "Shepherds" are the kings and rulers (2:8; 23:1-4). Instead of leading the flock, they will themselves be herded away by the wind (compare 4:11-12; 13:24).

decisions.choice: then: when the leaders and allies are gone
decisions.reason: The opening word stresses what follows: only when her support is swept away will the city feel the shame of her wickedness.

decisions.choice: leaders; allies
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures of shepherds and lovers stand for.

decisions.choice: Upepo utawachunga wachungaji wako
decisions.reason: Swahili can keep the Hebrew wordplay of "shepherd" and "shepherds" ("kuchunga", "wachungaji") at Literal; Balanced and Readable say what the wind does.

decisions.choice: "người chăn" (L, B); "nhà lãnh đạo" (R)
decisions.reason: The shepherds are the rulers, as in Jeremiah 2:8; Literal and Balanced keep the picture and its wordplay with "chăn", Readable names them.

source.text: יֹשַׁבְתְּ֙ בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן מְקֻנַּ֖נְתְּ בָּֽאֲרָזִ֑ים מַה־נֵּחַנְתְּ֙ בְּבֹא־לָ֣ךְ חֲבָלִ֔ים חִ֖יל כַּיֹּלֵדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [You] dwelling in the Lebanon, nested in the cedars, how you will groan in [the] coming to you [of] pangs, anguish like [one] giving birth!

en.L: You who dwell in Lebanon, \q nested among the cedars, \q how you will groan when pangs come upon you, \q anguish like [a woman] giving birth!
en.B: You who live in Lebanon, \q nesting among the cedars, \q how you will groan when the pains come on you, \q pain like a woman in labor!
en.R: You live in a palace made of cedar from Lebanon, \q snug as a bird in its nest. \q But how you will groan when pain comes on you, \q pain like a woman having a baby!

es.L: Tú que habitas en el Líbano, \q que anidas entre los cedros, \q ¡cómo gemirás cuando te vengan los dolores, \q angustia como de [mujer] que da a luz!
es.B: Tú que vives en el Líbano, \q que haces tu nido entre los cedros, \q ¡cómo gemirás cuando te lleguen los dolores, \q dolores como de mujer de parto!
es.R: Vives en un palacio hecho con cedros del Líbano, \q cómoda como un pájaro en su nido. \q ¡Pero cómo gemirás cuando te llegue el dolor, \q dolor como el de una mujer que está dando a luz!

fr.L: Toi qui habites le Liban, \q nichée dans les cèdres, \q comme tu gémiras quand les douleurs viendront sur toi, \q l’angoisse comme [celle d’une femme] qui enfante !
fr.B: Toi qui habites au Liban, \q qui fais ton nid dans les cèdres, \q comme tu gémiras quand les douleurs te saisiront, \q des douleurs comme celles d’une femme qui accouche !
fr.R: Tu habites dans un palais fait de cèdres du Liban, \q bien au chaud comme un oiseau dans son nid. \q Mais comme tu gémiras quand la douleur te saisira, \q une douleur comme celle d’une femme qui met un enfant au monde !

sw.L: Wewe ukaaye Lebanoni, \q uliyejenga kiota katika mierezi, \q jinsi utakavyougua uchungu utakapokujia, \q utungu kama wa [mwanamke] azaaye!
sw.B: Wewe unayeishi Lebanoni, \q unayejenga kiota katika mierezi, \q jinsi utakavyolia kwa uchungu utakapokujia, \q utungu kama wa mwanamke anayejifungua!
sw.R: Unaishi katika jumba lililojengwa kwa mierezi ya Lebanoni, \q umestarehe kama ndege katika kiota chake. \q Lakini jinsi utakavyolia kwa maumivu yatakapokujia, \q maumivu kama ya mwanamke anayezaa mtoto!

vi.L: Hỡi ngươi là kẻ ở trên Li-ban, \q làm tổ giữa các cây bá hương, \q ngươi sẽ rên siết biết bao khi cơn đau đến trên ngươi, \q đau đớn như [đàn bà] sinh nở!
vi.B: Hỡi ngươi là kẻ sống trên Li-ban, \q làm tổ giữa những cây bá hương, \q ngươi sẽ rên rỉ biết bao khi cơn đau ập đến, \q đau như người đàn bà chuyển dạ!
vi.R: Ngươi sống trong cung điện làm bằng gỗ bá hương Li-ban, \q ấm áp như chim trong tổ. \q Nhưng ngươi sẽ rên rỉ biết bao khi cơn đau ập đến, \q đau như người đàn bà sắp sinh con!

decisions.choice: dwelling in Lebanon, nested in the cedars: living in Jerusalem's cedar-built palaces
decisions.reason: Jerusalem is not in Lebanon; the words describe the city's royal buildings of Lebanon cedar (verses 6-7, 14-15; 1 Kings 7:2). Like a bird nesting high in a cedar, the city feels safe.

decisions.choice: how you will groan: the verb read as a form of "groan"
decisions.reason: The form is unusual. It is probably from the verb "to groan", which suits the picture of labor pains. Others take it from the verb "to be pitied": "how you will be pitied", or, said with irony, "how pitiable you will be".

decisions.choice: you dwelling, you nested: the forms read aloud
decisions.reason: The written forms have an older ending; the forms read aloud have the usual one. Both are "you", spoken to a woman, and the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: pangs like a woman giving birth: sudden, unavoidable anguish
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses the pains of labor for the terror of an enemy's coming (4:31; 6:24; 13:21).

decisions.choice: in a palace made of cedar from Lebanon; snug as a bird in its nest
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, since the city does not lie in Lebanon.

decisions.choice: "nichée" (L), feminine
decisions.reason: French shows that the one addressed is a woman, Jerusalem, as the Hebrew does; every level keeps the singular « tu » (Readable with feminine agreement in verses 21-22).

source.text: חַי־אָנִי֮ נְאֻם־יְהוָה֒ כִּ֣י אִם־יִהְיֶ֞ה כָּנְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה חוֹתָ֖ם עַל־יַ֣ד יְמִינִ֑י כִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶתְּקֶֽנְךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [As] I live, declares Yahweh, even if were Coniah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah a signet ring on [the] hand of my right, yet from there I would tear you off.

en.L: [As] I live, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand, yet from there I would tear you off.
en.B: As surely as I live, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, even if you were the signet ring on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand, I would still pull you off.
en.R: As surely as I live, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, even if you were the ring with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} seal on it, worn on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand, I would still pull you off.

es.L: Vivo yo, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que aunque Conías hijo de Joacim, rey de Judá, fuera anillo de sello en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano derecha, aun de allí te arrancaría.
es.B: Tan cierto como que yo vivo, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Conías hijo de Joacim, rey de Judá, aunque fueras el anillo de sello de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano derecha, aun así te arrancaría de allí.
es.R: Tan cierto como que yo vivo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Conías hijo de Joacim, rey de Judá, aunque fueras el anillo con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sello que llevo en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano derecha, aun así te arrancaría.

fr.L: [Aussi vrai que] je suis vivant, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, même si Conia fils de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, était un anneau à sceau à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main droite, de là je t’arracherais.
fr.B: Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Conia fils de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, même si tu étais l’anneau à sceau de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main droite, je t’en arracherais.
fr.R: Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Conia, fils de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, même si tu étais la bague qui porte {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sceau, à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main droite, je t’arracherais quand même.

sw.L: [Kama] niishivyo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hata kama Konia mwana wa Yehoyakimu, mfalme wa Yuda, angekuwa pete ya muhuri katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kuume, hata hivyo ningekung'oa kutoka huko.
sw.B: Hakika kama niishivyo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: Konia mwana wa Yehoyakimu, mfalme wa Yuda, hata kama ungekuwa pete ya muhuri katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia, ningekuvua tu.
sw.R: Hakika kama niishivyo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: Konia mwana wa Yehoyakimu, mfalme wa Yuda, hata kama ungekuwa pete yenye muhuri {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, ninayoivaa katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia, ningekuvua tu.

vi.L: [Thật như] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hằng sống, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, dù Cô-nia con trai Giê-hô-gia-kim, vua Giu-đa, có là chiếc nhẫn ấn trên tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ giật ngươi ra khỏi đó.
vi.B: Thật như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hằng sống, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy: Hỡi Cô-nia con trai Giê-hô-gia-kim, vua Giu-đa, dù ngươi có là chiếc nhẫn ấn trên tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ rút ngươi ra.
vi.R: Thật như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hằng sống, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Hỡi Cô-nia con trai Giê-hô-gia-kim, vua Giu-đa, dù ngươi có là chiếc nhẫn khắc con dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đeo trên tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ rút ngươi ra.

decisions.choice: Coniah son of Jehoiakim: the king also called Jehoiachin and Jeconiah
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim's son reigned three months in 597 BC before he was taken to Babylon (2 Kings 24:8-15). Kings calls him Jehoiachin; Jeremiah calls him Jeconiah (24:1; 27:20) and here, and in 22:28 and 37:1, Coniah, a short form of the name. Matthew 1:11-12 calls him Jechoniah. Each verse keeps the name its Hebrew uses.

decisions.choice: a signet ring on my right hand: something precious, kept close and used to act with the owner's full authority
decisions.reason: A signet ring was engraved with its owner's seal, pressed into clay or wax to sign documents (1 Kings 21:8; Esther 8:8). Even so close and valued a king would be torn off and thrown away.

decisions.choice: the signet ring: reversed in Haggai 2:23 for Coniah's grandson
decisions.reason: After the exile God tells Zerubbabel, grandson of Jeconiah (1 Chronicles 3:17-19), "I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you" (Haggai 2:23). The picture of rejection here is taken up there as a picture of restored favor to David's line.

decisions.choice: were Coniah ... I would tear you off: the speech turns from speaking about Coniah to speaking to him
decisions.reason: The sentence begins in the third person and ends in the second, as God turns to the king himself; verses 25-27 go on speaking to him.

decisions.choice: Coniah son of Jehoiakim ..., even if you were
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Coniah first and then say "you", so that the change from speaking about him to speaking to him does not confuse the reader.

decisions.choice: Conías
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the short form Coniah here; every level keeps "Conías", the same king as Jeconías (Matthew 1:11-12) and Joaquín (2 Kings 24-25), as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: Tan cierto como que yo vivo
decisions.reason: The oath on God's life is "Vivo yo" at Literal and "tan cierto como que yo vivo" at Balanced and Readable, as the Samuel note sets.

decisions.choice: Konia
decisions.reason: The verse's own short form of the king's name, kept as the Hebrew has it; he is the Yekonia and Yehoyakini of other books.

decisions.choice: "Conia"
decisions.reason: As the terms note: each verse keeps the form of the name its Hebrew uses (Coniah here, Jeconiah in 24:1), and the meaning decision says they are the same king.

decisions.choice: "Cô-nia" (Coniah)
decisions.reason: The verse keeps the short form of the name its Hebrew uses. It is new in Vietnamese, made like the published "Giê-chô-nia" (Matthew 1:11); meaning decision m1 says that he is the king called Jehoiachin and Jeconiah.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for Coniah at every level
decisions.reason: God turns to speak to the condemned king directly, with the "ngươi" of judgment used for Jehoiakim in verse 15.

source.text: וּנְתַתִּ֗יךָ בְּיַד֙ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וּבְיַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה יָג֖וֹר מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וּבְיַ֛ד נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּבְיַ֥ד הַכַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give you into [the] hand of [those] seeking your life, and into [the] hand of [those] whom you [are] fearful of their faces, and into [the] hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into [the] hand of the Chaldeans.

en.L: And I will give you into the hand of those who seek your life, and into the hand of those whom you dread, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
en.B: I will hand you over to those who want to kill you, to those you fear, to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
en.R: I will hand you over to the people who want to kill you, the people you are afraid of: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and the Babylonians.

es.L: Y te entregaré en mano de los que buscan tu vida, y en mano de aquellos de quienes tienes miedo, y en mano de Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y en mano de los caldeos.
es.B: Te entregaré en manos de los que quieren matarte, de aquellos a quienes temes, de Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y de los caldeos.
es.R: Te entregaré en manos de la gente que quiere matarte, la gente que te da miedo: Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y los babilonios.

fr.L: Et je te livrerai entre les mains de ceux qui en veulent à ta vie, et entre les mains de ceux devant qui tu trembles, et entre les mains de Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et entre les mains des Chaldéens.
fr.B: Je te livrerai à ceux qui veulent ta mort, à ceux que tu redoutes, à Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et aux Chaldéens.
fr.R: Je te livrerai aux gens qui veulent te tuer, aux gens dont tu as peur : Nabuchodonosor, le roi de Babylone, et les Babyloniens.

sw.L: Nami nitakutia mkononi mwa wale wanaotafuta uhai wako, na mkononi mwa wale unaowaogopa, na mkononi mwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, na mkononi mwa Wakaldayo.
sw.B: Nitakutia mikononi mwa wale wanaotaka kukuua, mikononi mwa wale unaowaogopa, mikononi mwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli na mikononi mwa Wakaldayo.
sw.R: Nitakutia mikononi mwa watu wanaotaka kukuua, watu unaowaogopa: Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli na Wababeli.

vi.L: Ta sẽ phó ngươi vào tay những kẻ tìm hại mạng sống ngươi, vào tay những kẻ ngươi sợ hãi, vào tay Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn và vào tay người Canh-đê.
vi.B: Ta sẽ phó ngươi vào tay những kẻ muốn giết ngươi, những kẻ ngươi khiếp sợ, là Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn và người Canh-đê.
vi.R: Ta sẽ phó ngươi vào tay những kẻ muốn giết ngươi, những kẻ ngươi sợ hãi: Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn và người Ba-by-lôn.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the spelling the Hebrew uses here for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Jeremiah mostly spells the name Nebuchadrezzar, closer to the Babylonian form; Kings and some chapters of Jeremiah spell it Nebuchadnezzar. It is the same king, who reigned 605-562 BC. Each verse keeps the form its Hebrew uses.

decisions.choice: those seeking your life: those who want to kill you
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" is to try to kill him (4:30; 11:21).

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the people of southern Babylonia whose dynasty ruled Babylon
decisions.reason: In Jeremiah the Chaldeans are the Babylonians and their army.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

decisions.choice: the people you are afraid of: Nebuchadrezzar ...
decisions.reason: Readable treats the last two names as saying who the feared enemies are, rather than repeating "into the hand of" four times.

source.text: וְהֵֽטַלְתִּ֣י אֹתְךָ֗ וְאֶֽת־אִמְּךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְלָדַ֔תְךָ עַ֚ל הָאָ֣רֶץ אַחֶ֔רֶת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֻלַּדְתֶּ֖ם שָׁ֑ם וְשָׁ֖ם תָּמֽוּתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will hurl you and your mother who bore you to the land another, where not you were born there, and there you will die.

en.L: And I will hurl you and your mother who bore you into another land, where you were not born, and there you will die.
en.B: I will throw you and the mother who gave birth to you into another country, where neither of you was born, and there you will both die.
en.R: I will throw you and your mother out into another country, where neither of you was born, and you will both die there.

es.L: Y te arrojaré a ti y a tu madre que te dio a luz a otra tierra, donde no {{plural_you:nacieron|nacisteis}}, y allí {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}.
es.B: Te arrojaré a ti y a la madre que te dio a luz a otro país, donde ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} nació, y allí {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}} los dos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} echaré a ti y a tu madre a otro país, donde ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} nació, y allí {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}} los dos.

fr.L: Et je te lancerai, toi et ta mère qui t’a enfanté, dans un autre pays, où vous n’êtes pas nés, et là vous mourrez.
fr.B: Je te jetterai, toi et la mère qui t’a mis au monde, dans un autre pays, où aucun de vous deux n’est né, et c’est là que vous mourrez tous les deux.
fr.R: Je te jetterai avec ta mère dans un autre pays, où aucun de vous deux n’est né, et vous y mourrez tous les deux.

sw.L: Nami nitakutupa wewe na mama yako aliyekuzaa mpaka nchi nyingine, ambayo hamkuzaliwa huko, na huko mtakufa.
sw.B: Nitakutupa wewe na mama aliyekuzaa mpaka nchi nyingine, ambayo hakuna kati yenu aliyezaliwa huko, nanyi nyote wawili mtakufa huko.
sw.R: Nitakutupa wewe na mama yako nje mpaka nchi nyingine, ambayo hakuna kati yenu aliyezaliwa huko, nanyi nyote wawili mtafia huko.

vi.L: Ta sẽ quăng ngươi và mẹ đã sinh ra ngươi sang một xứ khác, nơi các ngươi không được sinh ra, và các ngươi sẽ chết tại đó.
vi.B: Ta sẽ ném ngươi và người mẹ đã sinh ra ngươi sang một xứ khác, nơi không ai trong hai người được sinh ra, và cả hai sẽ chết tại đó.
vi.R: Ta sẽ ném ngươi và mẹ ngươi ra một xứ khác, nơi không ai trong hai người được sinh ra, và cả hai sẽ chết tại đó.

decisions.choice: your mother: Nehushta, the queen mother, taken to Babylon with her son
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 24:8, 12, 15 names her and says she went into exile with the king in 597 BC. The queen mother held a place of honor at court (13:18; 29:2).

decisions.choice: you were born, you will die: plural, the king and his mother together
decisions.reason: The last two verbs are plural, so both are meant.

decisions.choice: hurl: throw far, as one throws a spear
decisions.reason: The verb is used for flinging something away (1 Samuel 18:11; 20:33). The same verb returns in verse 28 and in 16:13.

decisions.choice: neither of you; you will both die
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the plural verbs include the king's mother.

source.text: וְעַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֛ם מְנַשְּׂאִ֥ים אֶת־נַפְשָׁ֖ם לָשׁ֣וּב שָׁ֑ם שָׁ֖מָּה לֹ֥א יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And to the land where they [are] lifting up their soul to return there, there not they will return.

en.L: But to the land to which they lift up their soul to return, there they will not return.
en.B: They will long to return to this land, but they will never come back to it.
en.R: They will long to come back home to this land, but they will never return.

es.L: Pero a la tierra a la que ellos anhelan con el alma volver, allá no volverán.
es.B: Anhelarán volver a esta tierra, pero nunca regresarán a ella.
es.R: Desearán con todas sus fuerzas regresar a casa, a esta tierra, pero nunca volverán.

fr.L: Mais au pays où ils élèvent leur âme pour y revenir, là ils ne reviendront pas.
fr.B: Ils désireront ardemment revenir dans ce pays, mais ils n’y reviendront jamais.
fr.R: Ils auront très envie de rentrer chez eux, dans ce pays, mais ils n’y reviendront jamais.

sw.L: Lakini nchi ile ambayo wanaiinulia nafsi zao kurudi, huko hawatarudi.
sw.B: Watatamani sana kurudi katika nchi hii, lakini hawatarudi huku kamwe.
sw.R: Watatamani sana kurudi nyumbani katika nchi hii, lakini hawatarudi kamwe.

vi.L: Nhưng xứ mà linh hồn chúng khao khát trở về, chúng sẽ không được trở về đó.
vi.B: Chúng sẽ khao khát trở về xứ này, nhưng sẽ chẳng bao giờ được trở về.
vi.R: Chúng sẽ mong mỏi được trở về quê hương này, nhưng sẽ không bao giờ trở về được.

decisions.choice: lift up their soul: long for, set their desire on
decisions.reason: To lift up one's soul to something is to long for it with all one's being (44:14; Deuteronomy 24:15).

decisions.choice: they: the king and his mother, and those taken with them
decisions.reason: The verse moves to "they", speaking about the exiles rather than to the king.

decisions.choice: the longing comes first (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with "the land" for emphasis; Balanced and Readable begin with the longing and end with the refusal, which keeps the stress on "never".

source.text: הַעֶ֨צֶב נִבְזֶ֜ה נָפ֗וּץ הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ כָּנְיָ֔הוּ אִ֨ם־כְּלִ֔י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֤וּעַ הֽוּטֲלוּ֙ ה֣וּא וְזַרְע֔וֹ וְהֻ֨שְׁלְכ֔וּ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָדָֽעוּ׃

decisions.choice: a pot, a vessel: a cheap clay jar, smashed and thrown out
decisions.reason: The first word is rare and seems to name a clay pot or figure; the second is the common word for a jar or dish. A cracked clay pot was simply thrown away (19:11; 48:38; Hosea 8:8).

decisions.choice: the questions: a lament that asks how the king could come to this
decisions.reason: The first questions ask whether Coniah is no more than a worthless pot; the third asks why he is cast out. They read as the people's grief and bewilderment, which verses 29-30 answer with the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: his offspring: his children and descendants
decisions.reason: Coniah was eighteen when he was exiled (2 Kings 24:8); 1 Chronicles 3:17-18 lists sons born to him, probably in Babylon. The word covers all his line, which verse 30 speaks of again.

decisions.choice: children (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "offspring"; here Balanced and Readable say "children", and in verse 30, where the line of kings is meant, "descendants".

decisions.choice: land, land, land: the threefold call makes the summons as solemn as possible
decisions.reason: Repeating a word three times gives the greatest stress (7:4; Isaiah 6:3). The land is called as a witness to the sentence that follows.

decisions.choice: land: the land of Judah, or the whole earth
decisions.reason: The word can mean a country or the earth. Since the oracle concerns Judah's king and his exile from the land, it most likely means the land of Judah; the earth may also be called to witness (6:19; Isaiah 1:2).

decisions.choice: "Pays" (B, R); "Terre" (L)

decisions.choice: write this man childless: list him as having no heir to the throne; none of his line will reign
decisions.reason: The picture is of a register of citizens or of a royal line (Numbers 1:18; Ezekiel 13:9). Coniah did have sons (1 Chronicles 3:17-18; verse 28 above), so "childless" does not mean he would have no children: it means that, as king, he is entered as one with no successor, because none of his descendants will sit on David's throne. No son of his ever reigned; his grandson Zerubbabel later governed Judah under Persia, but not as king (Haggai 1:1).

decisions.choice: the line of Coniah and the line of the Messiah: Matthew 1:11-12 lists Jechoniah among the ancestors of Jesus through Joseph
decisions.reason: Matthew traces the royal line from David through Jechoniah and Zerubbabel to Joseph, the husband of Mary. Christians have read this together with Jeremiah's word in several ways: that Jesus inherits the royal title through Joseph as his legal father without being Coniah's physical descendant; that Luke 3:27-31 traces another line through David's son Nathan; or that God's promise to Zerubbabel (Haggai 2:23) shows the sentence on Coniah's line was later lifted. The text of Jeremiah itself speaks of the kings of Coniah's own day and after.

decisions.choice: prosper: succeed, achieve what one sets out to do
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: Coniah will not succeed in his own lifetime, and none of his line will succeed in reaching the throne.

decisions.choice: in the records as if he had no children
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the register and that "childless" means without an heir to the throne (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: (L); The LORD says this: (B); This is what the LORD says: (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for this formula, as in verse 3.
